text:
jordan: Quick follow-up from the rate-limiter sync — proposing a small refactor: introduce a lightweight "credit-slicing" layer between admission and token buckets so we can support cooperative tenant borrowing and safer soft-shed behavior. sketch below.

ana: can you sketch the invariants we need to preserve? fairness, no extra headroom for abuse, and predictable p95s.

jordan: sure — main invariants: 1) per-tenant steady-state allocation must not drop below committed reservation; 2) borrowed credits are time-limited and observed in telemetry; 3) admission decision still enforces short-term latency SLOs (reject vs queue).

sam: sounds neat, but how do we avoid an attacker spinning many small tenants to game borrowing?

jordan: plan includes a cheap abuse filter: require a short warmup window and connect borrowing eligibility to an abuse score and historical success rate. small tenants under a threshold can't borrow beyond tiny amounts.

mike: what telemetry do we need to validate this in prod? exact metrics + dashboards please.

jordan: at minimum: borrow_rate per-tenant, borrow_latency p50/p95, effective_tokens_consumed (borrowed vs reserved), borrow_reject_count, scaling_events triggered by borrow. also a global "credit-pool-utilization" gauge and flux logs for handoffs.

lee: implementation question — do we plumb credit-slicing into the existing lease service or implement as an admission-side shim?

jordan: prefer admission-side shim to keep lease contracts minimal. shim answers: allocate_slice(request), commit_slice(response), refund_slice(on_abort). shim communicates with optional coordinator for cross-tenant borrowing.

ana: how will we migrate existing Dedicated workloads without changing tokens? we need backwards compat.

jordan: default: shim off. migration path: 1) enable shim read-only (telemetry only), 2) enable local-only borrowing for non-reserved tenants, 3) staggered enable for reserved tenants with opt-in flags, 4) full rollout with auto-fallback to old path.

tara: oncall: what failures look like? if coordinator dies do we fail closed or open?

jordan: fail-safe is fail-closed for borrow attempts (no extra tokens), but continue serving from reserved capacity. we add circuit-breaker and degrade to per-tenant token buckets only.

sam: and rate-limits and quotas — do we need any new audit logs for compliance? banks will want traceability.

jordan: yes: every borrow event must be auditable: tenant_id, amount, source_decision (policy_id), parent_request_id, timestamp, and resolved expiry. store to short-term retention + indices.

mike: love the audit idea. also suggest a synthetic experiment: create 50 synthetic tenants with spiky load and run trials under normal and degraded coordinator to see tail impact.

jordan: agreed. experiment plan: create two cohorts (with/without borrowing), run a 6-hour burn with random spikes, collect latency, cost-per-token, borrow_success_rate. roll into canary.

lee: small nit — data model for slices: {slice_id, tenant_id, amount, expiry_ts, origin_policy, borrow_parent_id?}. will be a single-line protobuf.

jordan: yes that's the proto. sample: ```proto
message CreditSlice {
  string slice_id = 1;
  string tenant = 2;
  int64 amount = 3;
  int64 expiry_unix = 4;
  string policy = 5;
  string parent_slice = 6;
}
```

ana: doesn't that risk state explosion if we create lots of tiny slices for every request?

jordan: we coalesce slices per-tenant per-window (e.g., 100ms window) and only materialize if borrowing occurs. most traffic keeps using local token bucket.

infra-bot: CI checks: branch credit-slicing-probe passes unit tests, lint OK, mock-load integration failing on borrow backpressure test (flaky) — see link: https://ci.redwood.internal/1234

mike: can we add a probabilistic admission knob to limit borrow QPS globally during high load? helps graceful global backpressure.

jordan: yes expose a global borrow-rate-cap with adaptive shrink on high CPU or high KV-latency. default high but tuned in canaries.

tara: also, need runbook snippet for when borrow coordinator causes client-visible 429s. include how to cutover to no-borrow mode.

jordan: will draft runbook: steps to flip feature flag, rollback coordinator, and run a short rolling restart of shim clients.

sam: one last concern — billing alignment. Borrowing can shift cost to other tenants. how do we ensure billing isn't surprising?

jordan: borrow accounting: mark borrowed consumption separately and bill back to borrower at a premium or charge to the peak-reserved tenant if policy says so. configurable per-tenant. billing team needs hooks.

mike: next steps?

jordan: I'll open a short RFC PR with design, telemetry schema, migration checklist, and experiment plan. tagging infra + platform. please review in 48h. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

lee: ack, will review the proto and shim patch.

ana: will review invariants and abuse filters.

sam: will model attacker scenarios and give numbers.

infra-bot: reminder: meeting "Rate-limiter followup" scheduled in 2 days at 10:00 — add notes to RFC PR.
